items.title: The azimuthal line field $\rho^{-1}e_\varphi$: local integrability and distributional curl on the axis
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $Z:=\{(0,0,x_3):x_3\in\mathbb R\}\subset\mathbb R^3$ be the third coordinate axis and let
$$f:\mathbb R^3\setminus Z\to\mathbb R^3,\qquad f(x)=\frac{(-x_2,\ x_1,\ 0)}{x_1^2+x_2^2},\qquad x=(x_1,x_2,x_3),$$
so that, in cylindrical notation $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$ and $e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0)$, one has $f=e_\varphi/\rho$ on the punctured space. Let $T_f$ be the regular distribution of $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and let $A$ be the $\mathbb R^3$-valued distribution
$$A(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,x_3)\,dx_3,\qquad\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),$$
the third-direction line measure on $Z$. For an $\mathbb R^3$-valued distribution $T=(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ whose components are scalar distributions of [[def-distribution]], the pairings used below are the componentwise readings of [[def-distributional-derivative]]:
$$\langle\operatorname{div}T,\varphi\rangle:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\langle T_i,\partial_i\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}T,\psi\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\langle T_i,(\operatorname{curl}\psi)_i\rangle .$$
Then: (a) $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$; (b) $\operatorname{div}f=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}f=0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3\setminus Z$; (c) for every vector test $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and every scalar test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$,
$$\langle\operatorname{curl}T_f,\psi\rangle=2\pi\,A(\psi),\qquad \langle\operatorname{div}T_f,\varphi\rangle=0,$$
that is, $\operatorname{curl}T_f=2\pi\,e_3\,\delta_Z$ and $\operatorname{div}T_f=0$ in the distributional sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]; and (d) for every $r>0$ and $h\in\mathbb R$, the circulation of $f$ along the positively oriented circle $\gamma_{r,h}:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R^3\setminus Z$, $\gamma_{r,h}(t)=(r\cos t,r\sin t,h)$, traversed once with increasing $t$, is $2\pi$ ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]], read componentwise). No product of distributions is formed.
items.strategy: Direct: Tonelli axis nullity, compactly restricted polar integrability, annular excision with outward inner normal -e_rho, dominated convergence and uniform continuity, vanishing divergence flux, and the once-traversed increasing-t circle gamma_r,h in Proof 1.3. Countable Choice is inherited through the stated mathematical suppliers.

items.title: The piecewise constant cylinder field $e_3\mathbf 1_{\{\rho<a\}}$: distributional curl on the cylinder
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a>0$, write $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ and $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$, let
$$S:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\rho=a\}$$
be the circular cylinder of radius $a$ about the third coordinate axis, with unit normal $e_\rho=\rho^{-1}(x_1,x_2,0)$ pointing from the interior region $\{\rho<a\}$ to the exterior region $\{\rho>a\}$, and let $e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0)$ and $e_3=(0,0,1)$. Let $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be the piecewise constant field
$$g(x):=\begin{cases}e_3,&\rho<a,\\ 0,&\rho>a,\end{cases}$$
extended arbitrarily on the three-dimensional Lebesgue-null set $S$, and let $T_g$ be its regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). For an $\mathbb R^3$-valued distribution $T=(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ whose components are scalar distributions of [[def-distribution]], a scalar test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and a vector test $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, the pairings used below are the componentwise readings of [[def-distributional-derivative]]:
$$\langle\operatorname{div}T,\varphi\rangle:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\langle T_i,\partial_i\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}T,\psi\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\langle T_i,(\operatorname{curl}\psi)_i\rangle .$$
Then for every vector test $\psi$ and every scalar test $\varphi$,
$$\langle\operatorname{curl}T_g,\psi\rangle=\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS,\qquad \langle\operatorname{div}T_g,\varphi\rangle=0,$$
that is, $\operatorname{curl}T_g=e_\varphi\,\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{div}T_g=0$ in the distributional sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]. The surface integral is that of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; since $\psi$ has compact support it equals the integral over any compact cylinder segment containing $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap S$. Equivalently, with $g_\pm$ the one-sided values and the normal $e_\rho$ from the minus to the plus side, $g_+-g_-=-e_3$, $e_\rho\times(g_+-g_-)=e_\varphi$ and $e_\rho\cdot(g_+-g_-)=0$. No product of distributions is formed.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; the nullity of the cylinder surface, the divergence theorem on the cylinder, and two coordinate computations.

1.1 The cylinder $S=\{x:x_1^2+x_2^2=a^2\}$ is closed, hence Borel. For each $(x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb R^2$, its section $S^{(x_2,x_3)}:=\{x_1\in\mathbb R:(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in S\}$ consists of at most the two values $\pm\sqrt{a^2-x_2^2}$ when $|x_2|\le a$, and is empty otherwise. Each section is $\lambda_1$-null by [F4]. Tonelli and product-measure agreement [F4] give $\lambda_3(S)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\lambda_1(S^{(x_2,x_3)})\,d\lambda_2=0$. [given, F4]

2.1 The bounded Borel function $g_0:=e_3\mathbf 1_{\{\rho<a\}}$ agrees with $g$ off the null set $S$ of step 1.1, so completeness [F5] makes $g$ Lebesgue measurable with the same almost-everywhere class as $g_0$; by [F5] this class is locally integrable. Hence $T_g:=T_{g_0}$ is a well-defined distribution by [F2], and for the tests of [F1] the componentwise pairings of [F3] read $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_g,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g_0\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi\,d\lambda_3$ and $\langle\operatorname{div}T_g,\varphi\rangle=-\int_{\mathbb R^3}g_0\cdot\nabla\varphi\,d\lambda_3$, where the componentwise sums against the vector tests are the ordinary finite sums of the stated integrals. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 Choose $R>a$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cup\operatorname{supp}\varphi\subset W:=\{\rho<R,\ |x_3|<R\}$ and put $V:=\{\rho<a,\ |x_3|<R\}$. Since $\operatorname{curl}\psi$ and $\nabla\varphi$ are supported in $W$, and $g_0$ equals $e_3$ on $V$, equals $0$ on the open set $W\setminus\overline V$, and the remaining part $W\cap\partial V$ lies in the null set $S$ of step 1.1, the two integrals of step 2.1 reduce to integrals over $V$: $\int_{\mathbb R^3}g_0\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi\,d\lambda_3=\int_V e_3\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi\,d\lambda_3$ and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}g_0\cdot\nabla\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\int_V e_3\cdot\nabla\varphi\,d\lambda_3$. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The field $F_0:=\varphi e_3$ is $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$, hence on a neighborhood of $\overline V$, and by [F9] its divergence is $\operatorname{div}F_0=\partial_3\varphi=e_3\cdot\nabla\varphi$. The divergence theorem [F7] on the presentation [F6] gives $\int_V e_3\cdot\nabla\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial V}\varphi\,e_3\cdot\nu\,dS$. On the lateral face $\nu=e_\rho$ and $e_3\cdot e_\rho=0$ by [F8]; on the two disc caps $x_3=\pm R$ the test $\varphi$ vanishes because $\operatorname{supp}\varphi\subset\{|x_3|<R\}$; hence $\int_V e_3\cdot\nabla\varphi\,d\lambda_3=0$. With steps 2.1 and 3.1 this proves $\langle\operatorname{div}T_g,\varphi\rangle=0$ for every scalar test. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F6, F7, F8, F9]

4.2 The field $G_0:=\psi\times e_3$ is $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$, and by [F8] its coordinates are $G_0=(\psi_2,-\psi_1,0)$, so by [F9] $\operatorname{div}G_0=\partial_1\psi_2-\partial_2\psi_1=(\operatorname{curl}\psi)_3=e_3\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi$. The divergence theorem [F7] on the presentation [F6] gives $\int_V e_3\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi\,d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial V}G_0\cdot\nu\,dS$. The disc caps carry $\psi=0$ by the support condition, while on the lateral face $\nu=e_\rho$ and $G_0\cdot e_\rho=(\psi\times e_3)\cdot e_\rho=\psi\cdot e_\varphi$ by [F8]; therefore $\int_V e_3\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi\,d\lambda_3=\int_{\rho=a,\ |x_3|<R}e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$, and by [F10] the last integral equals $\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ because $e_\varphi\cdot\psi$ is compactly supported and vanishes off the compact band $\{\rho=a,\ |x_3|\le R\}$. With steps 2.1 and 3.1 this is $\langle\operatorname{curl}T_g,\psi\rangle=\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ for every vector test, which is the claimed identification $\operatorname{curl}T_g=e_\varphi\,\delta_S$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10]

5.1 The one-sided values of $g$ across $S$ are $g_+=0$ and $g_-=e_3$, so $g_+-g_-=-e_3$ and, by [F8], $e_\rho\times(g_+-g_-)=e_\rho\times(-e_3)=e_\varphi$ and $e_\rho\cdot(g_+-g_-)=e_\rho\cdot(-e_3)=0$, which is the stated equivalence. The two distributional identities of steps 4.1 and 4.2 involve only integrals of locally integrable functions against smooth tests, so no product of two distributions is formed anywhere; the only multiplication on $S$ is that of the compactly supported function $e_\varphi\cdot\psi$ with the surface measure of [F10]. Countable Choice is used in step 1.1 through the product-measure and finite-null-set suppliers [F4] and is inherited only through the cited measure, surface and distribution interfaces [F11]; no stronger choice principle occurs. [step 4.1, step 4.2, F2, F4, F8, F10, F11] ∎

items.title: Divergence and curl of the Newtonian potential of a smooth compact vector field
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and define componentwise
$$A_i(x):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f_i(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^3,$$
so that $A=N(f)$ componentwise with the Newtonian-potential transform $N$ of [[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]] and [[def-newtonian-potential]]. Then $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, both integrals below are absolutely convergent for every $x$, and for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$
$$\operatorname{div}A(x)=N(\operatorname{div}f)(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{(\operatorname{div}f)(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$
$$\operatorname{curl}A(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$
The curl identity needs no divergence-free hypothesis and holds pointwise at every point of $\mathbb R^3$, including points of the support of $f$; the kernel is differentiated, its smoothness at the pole is not assumed. Countable Choice is inherited from the smooth Newtonian supplier and the polar-coordinate and surface-measure interfaces of the estimates.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** the componentwise derivative identity of the smooth Newtonian upgrade, then a finite excision (spherical shell) integration by parts and one dominated limit.

1.1 Since each $f_i$ is smooth and compactly supported, [F2] gives $A_i=N(f_i)\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $D^\alpha A_i=N(D^\alpha f_i)$ for every multi-index $\alpha$; in particular $A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ by [F3], and $\partial_iA_i=N(\partial_if_i)$ for each $i$. Summing over $i$ and using finite additivity of the integral [F8], $\operatorname{div}A=\sum_i\partial_iA_i=N(\sum_i\partial_if_i)=N(\operatorname{div}f)$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$, which is the first displayed identity; its integral is absolutely convergent because $|\operatorname{div}f|\le\|\operatorname{div}f\|_\infty$ is bounded and compactly supported and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-1}d\lambda_3<+\infty$ by [F7]. [given, F1, F2, F3, F7, F8]

1.2 Fix $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and $j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$, and choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subset B_R(x)$. For $0<\varepsilon<R$ let $\Omega_\varepsilon:=B_R(x)\setminus\overline{B_\varepsilon(x)}$, presented as in [F5]. On a neighborhood of the compact closure the scalar product $y\mapsto f_k(y)\Phi(x-y)$ is $C^1$, and by [F4] its partial derivative is $\partial_{y_j}(f_k\Phi(x-y))=(\partial_jf_k)(y)\Phi(x-y)+f_k(y)\partial_{y_j}\Phi(x-y)$. Applying the divergence theorem [F5] to the field $f_k\Phi(x-\cdot)e_j$ on $\Omega_\varepsilon$ gives $\int_{\Omega_\varepsilon}(\partial_jf_k)\Phi(x-y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\partial B_R(x)}f_k\Phi(x-y)(\nu_R)_j\,dS+\int_{\partial B_\varepsilon(x)}f_k\Phi(x-y)(\nu_\varepsilon)_j\,dS-\int_{\Omega_\varepsilon}f_k(y)\partial_{y_j}\Phi(x-y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$. The outer sphere contributes $0$ because $f=0$ there; the inner sphere term is bounded in absolute value, by [F8] and the bound $|\Phi|=1/(4\pi|y-x|)=1/(4\pi\varepsilon)$ there, by $\|f_k\|_\infty\frac1{4\pi\varepsilon}\,|\partial B_\varepsilon(x)|=\|f_k\|_\infty\frac{|S^2|}{4\pi}\varepsilon\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$ by [F6]. [given, F4, F5, F6, F8]

2.1 Let $\varepsilon\to0$ in the identity of step 1.2. The shell integrands $(\partial_jf_k)\Phi(x-y)\mathbf 1_{\Omega_\varepsilon}$ are dominated on $B_R(x)$ by $\|\partial_jf_k\|_\infty|\Phi|$, and the shell integrands $f_k\partial_{y_j}\Phi(x-y)\mathbf 1_{\Omega_\varepsilon}$ by $\|f_k\|_\infty|\partial_{y_j}\Phi|\le\|f_k\|_\infty\frac{1}{4\pi}|x-y|^{-2}$; both majorants are integrable on $B_R(x)$ by [F7], and both families converge pointwise off the null singleton $\{x\}$ to the corresponding unrestricted integrands. Dominated convergence [F9] therefore gives $\int_{B_R(x)}(\partial_jf_k)\Phi(x-y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=-\int_{B_R(x)}f_k(y)\partial_{y_j}\Phi(x-y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$; the left side is $N(\partial_jf_k)(x)=\partial_jA_k(x)$ by step 1.1, and since $\partial_{y_j}\Phi(x-y)=\frac{x_j-y_j}{4\pi|x-y|^3}$ for $y\ne x$, this reads $\partial_jA_k(x)=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f_k(y)(x_j-y_j)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy$, the integral being absolutely convergent because $|f_k(y)(x_j-y_j)|\le\|f_k\|_\infty|x-y|$ on $B_R(x)$ and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}d\lambda_3<+\infty$ by [F7]. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F4, F7, F9]

3.1 Summing the identity of step 2.1 with the alternating symbol, $(\operatorname{curl}A)_i=\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_jA_k=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\varepsilon_{ijk}f_k(y)(x_j-y_j)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{(f(y)\times(x-y))_i}{|x-y|^3}\,dy$ by the component identity of [F10] and finite linearity of the integral [F8]; as this holds for each $i$, $\operatorname{curl}A(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy$, and the integral is absolutely convergent because $|f(y)\times(x-y)|\le\|f\|_\infty|x-y|$ and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}<+\infty$ by [F7]. With step 1.1 this proves both displayed identities at the arbitrary point $x$; the point was allowed to lie in $\operatorname{supp}f$, since the excision argument only removed a ball around it and used the bound on the differentiated kernel, so no smoothness of the kernel at the pole is assumed. Countable Choice is used only through the polar and surface-measure interfaces [F11] and the stated choice assumption of the smooth-newtonian supplier, and no stronger principle occurs. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F7, F8, F10, F11] ∎

items.title: The steady-current (magnetostatic) regime, the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal noncompact models
items.statement:
For the Lebesgue/surface/distributional source and admissibility branches (c)-(d), assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The smooth formulation in (a) and the smooth conserved-current predicate in (b) do not themselves use Choice. Let the laboratory region and its chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and fix $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

**(a) [Steady-current regime].** A steady-current (magnetostatic) configuration on $\Omega\times I$ consists of a field pair $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and source fields $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that are independent of $t$ and satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For such a configuration the formal distributional branch of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\operatorname{div}J=0$ distributionally; this is pointwise when $J$ is $C^1$. In the jointly $C^2$ field/$C^1$ source branch its classical proof applies directly. The locally integrable distributional reading here inherits Countable Choice, whereas the stated classical $C^2/C^1$ compatibility calculation is choice-free, and the four adopted equations are equivalent to the electrostatic pair and the magnetostatic pair
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J .$$

**(b) [Compact smooth current class].** The compact smooth current class of this framework consists of the currents $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. A magnetostatic field of such a current is a field $B$ of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with the extended $J$. This is the hypothesis class of the vector-potential, Biot-Savart and dipole theorems of this page; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of $B$ in the class.

**(c) [Ideal source objects].** Define three ideal current source objects outside the compact class, together with the data selecting their fields. Curve parameters $s$ and $L$ and the radius $a$ carry metres; the signed line-current amplitude $I$ carries amperes and the signed sheet-current amplitude $K$ carries A m$^{-1}$. The field $B$ carries tesla, as in [[def-em-si-conventions]].

**(c1) [Closed thin loop].** For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ ($L>0$) and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal loop current is the distribution
$$\langle J_\gamma,\psi\rangle:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),$$
with $\rho_\gamma:=0$.

**(c2) [Infinite straight wire].** For $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal wire current is
$$\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle:=I\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,s)\,ds,$$
with $\rho_{\rm w}:=0$.

**(c3) [Infinite cylindrical sheet].** For $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$, $e_\rho:=\rho^{-1}(x_1,x_2,0)$ and $e_\varphi:=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0)$ on $\{\rho>0\}$, and $K\in\mathbb R$, the ideal solenoid sheet current is
$$\langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$$
([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], read on compact cylinder segments), with $\rho_S:=0$. All three pairings are finite because $\psi$ has compact support.

**(c4) [Admissibility].** A field $B$ is admitted for one of these declared models when: $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ (hence a distribution by [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $C^1$ off the support of the current; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ hold pointwise off that support; the distributional identities $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold against every scalar divergence test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and vector curl test $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in the sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]; $B$ has the model's declared symmetry: in (c2) and (c3), $B(x+he_3)=B(x)$ for every $h\in\mathbb R$, and $B(R_\theta x)=R_\theta B(x)$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$, at off-source points, where $R_\theta(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x_1\cos\theta-x_2\sin\theta,x_1\sin\theta+x_2\cos\theta,x_3)$; no symmetry is required in (c1); and $B$ obeys the decay requirement: $|B(x)|\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in (c1), and in (c2), (c3), $\sup_{(\theta,z)\in C}|B(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta,z)|\to0$ as $r\to\infty$ for every nonempty compact $C\subset\mathbb R^2$. The companion examples exhibit and verify the fields of the two axisymmetric models in this class; the definition itself asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite energy or limiting relation for the declared models, and no compact-class theorem of this page applies to them.

**(d) [Scope].** This is a model restriction: the steady-current regime for compact smooth currents, and three explicitly declared ideal noncompact or singular models. It excludes point charges, weaker-regularity volume sources, moving sheets, normal sheet currents and any claim of empirical exactness; the equations in (c4) define a mathematical admissibility predicate; its physical adoption for these source objects is a separate postulate, and no product of distributions is formed.
items.strategy: Formulation and well-definedness checks. items.title: The magnetic dipole moment of a compact conserved current and of the declared ideal thin loop
items.statement:
Let the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal models be those of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

**(a) [Compact smooth currents].** Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. The **magnetic dipole moment** of $J$ is the vector
$$m:=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3,$$
of unit A m$^2$. The integral is computed componentwise over any nondegenerate closed bounding rectangle $Q$ containing $\operatorname{supp}J$, using the continuous functions $y\mapsto(y\times J(y))_i$ on $Q$ and their zero extension outside $Q$. Its value is independent of the chosen larger bounding rectangle by finite rectangular subdivision and vanishing of the integrand off its support; the support itself need not be Jordan measurable. Thus this is a Riemann integral of continuous compactly supported functions ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); it is absolutely finite because $J$ is bounded with compact support.

**(b) [Declared ideal thin loop].** For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ and $I\in\mathbb R$, the **magnetic moment** of the ideal loop current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) is
$$m:=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds,$$
again a componentwise Riemann integral over the compact interval $[0,L]$ of continuous functions; for the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ traversed in the positive orientation this is $m=I\pi a^2e_3$.

**(c) [Status and scope].** In both clauses $m$ is a source moment of the declared current model: it is not a rest mass, not an intrinsic spin and not an observed quantity. The definition asserts no far-field property of $m$ (that is the content of [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]] under its hypotheses), no agreement between the two clauses in a common limit, and no moment for currents outside the two classes; no higher multipole is defined here. The finite Riemann moment definitions and circular-loop evaluation themselves are choice-free; no distribution-embedding or surface-measure theorem is used to compute these moments.
items.strategy: Two type definitions with their well-definedness checks. (a) The map $y\mapsto y\times J(y)$ is continuous on every closed bounding rectangle $Q$ containing its support and vanishes off that support, so each component is Riemann integrable on $Q$ ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]); boundedness on $Q$ makes the integral absolutely finite. For two bounding rectangles take a common larger rectangle and subdivide it at their face coordinates; all extra cells have zero integrand off the support, so finite additivity identifies both values without integrating over the support itself, and the units follow from $y$ in metres and $J$ in A m$^{-2}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). (b) $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are continuous on the compact circle and their cross product is periodic, so the componentwise integral over $[0,L]$ exists; for the circle $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ and $\int_0^{2\pi a}ae_3\,ds=2\pi a^2e_3$, giving $m=I\pi a^2e_3$. (c) records the status: the moment is a model quantity of an idealised source, and its far-field interpretation belongs to [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]]; no measurement, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. The displayed finite Riemann computations use no Choice axiom. The physical/distributional interpretations of source models retain their separately stated premises.

items.title: Coulomb-gauge Newtonian vector potential for a compact smooth conserved current
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** componentwise reduction to the Newtonian-potential lemma and the standard second-derivative vector identities. 1.1 For each $i$ the datum $J_i$ is smooth and compactly supported, so [[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]] gives $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $D^\alpha A_i=\mu_0N(D^\alpha J_i)$ for every multi-index $\alpha$ and $-\Delta A_i=\mu_0J_i$ pointwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); hence (a). 2.1 Take $\alpha=e_i$ in the same derivative identity. Since $\operatorname{div}J=\sum_i\partial_iJ_i=0$ and $N$ is componentwise linear, $$\operatorname{div}A=\sum_i\partial_iA_i=\mu_0\sum_iN(\partial_iJ_i)=\mu_0N(\operatorname{div}J)=0$$ pointwise ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); this is (b), and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ is used nowhere else. 3.1 $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ is $C^\infty$ because $A$ is. Then $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}A=0$ by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]], and $$\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=\nabla(\operatorname{div}A)-\Delta A=\mu_0J$$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]] combined with (b) and (a). This is the pointwise magnetostatic pair of (c). 3.2 Reading (c) inside the framework: [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](a) identifies the magnetostatic pair as the reduction of the adopted equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] when $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=0$, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: choose $E=\rho=0$ and extend $B,J$ independently of time; the electrostatic identities and both time derivatives then vanish. Alternatively a given compatible electrostatic pair supplies them. No unspecified electric field or charge density is being asserted to exist (the identity $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ is not used in this item). 3.3 (d) is scope bookkeeping: the gauge freedom and homogeneous solutions are not analysed here, and no claim is extended beyond the compact smooth class. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument.

items.title: Biot-Savart representation for a compact smooth conserved current and its declared thin-loop limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ be a compact smooth current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Biot-Savart integral represents the field,
$$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$
Moreover the same formula holds in the declared thin-loop limit, constructed in the all-space laboratory $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$: if $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ is a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$), $I\in\mathbb R$, and $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are the mollified divergence-free compact currents of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] associated with the tangent line current of $\gamma$, then their fields (given by the displayed formula with $J:=j_\varepsilon$) converge, with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$, to
$$B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds,$$
a locally integrable global distributional field with $\operatorname{div}B_\gamma=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B_\gamma=\mu_0J_\gamma$, smoothness off the curve and decay at spatial infinity, hence the admitted field of the declared ideal thin loop under [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]. Its almost-everywhere representative on $\mathbb R^3$ is supplied by [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]], independently of the away-from-curve convergence. Nothing is asserted on the wire, about line self-energy, about the infinite-wire or sheet models, or for currents outside the compact smooth class and its declared thin-loop limit.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** the differentiated-kernel identity of [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]], then the thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]]. 1.1 By [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)$. Applying [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]] to $f:=J$ and multiplying by $\mu_0$ gives, at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$ The integral is absolutely convergent: $|J(y)\times(x-y)|\le\|J\|_\infty|x-y|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]) and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}\,d\lambda_3<+\infty$, the estimate supplied by [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]]; this proves the first assertion at every point, including points of the support. 2.1 Thin-loop limit: [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] states that the tangent distribution $j$ of the closed curve has $\operatorname{div}j=0$, that the mollified currents $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, and that their Biot-Savart fields converge with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$ to the displayed loop integral. By step 1.1 with $J:=j_\varepsilon$ (each $j_\varepsilon$ is a compact smooth conserved current) the field of $j_\varepsilon$ is exactly its displayed Biot-Savart integral; hence the limit is the field of the declared ideal thin loop of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1). The strengthened supplier separately proves global local integrability, the two distributional identities, off-curve smoothness and decay; these establish all clauses of admissibility in [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). The physical reading is the explicit adoption [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]. The every-derivative compact convergence remains an additional away-from-curve conclusion and is not used to deduce a global distributional identity. 2.2 Scope: the statement is confined to the compact smooth class and its declared thin-loop limit; no formula is asserted for noncompact currents (the infinite-wire model is verified separately on the companion examples page), and no near-wire, self-energy or radiation claim is made. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument. The thin-loop construction uses the all-space laboratory Omega=R3, so every compact mollified loop current satisfies the smooth-current domain condition.

items.title: Far-field dipole expansion of a compact conserved current with a uniform explicit remainder
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$ for some $a>0$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, and let $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ be the magnetic moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a). Then for $r=|x|\ge2a$, uniformly in the unit vector $n=x/r$,
$$A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^3}\right),\qquad B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^4}\right),$$
where $\|J\|_1=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|J|\,d\lambda_3$ and the constants implicit in the $O$ terms are absolute: one constant works for all $r\ge2a$ and all unit $n$. This is a controlled two-term far-field estimate: nothing is asserted for $r<2a$ or at the support, no higher multipole is defined here, and the leading dipole term is not claimed to be exact.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** transport of the explicit uniform-remainder lemma to the framework's objects. 1.1 The hypotheses of [[lem-em-magnetic-dipole-remainder]] are exactly those stated here for $J$ (smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free, contained in $B_a(0)$), and the objects of that lemma, $A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int J(y)|x-y|^{-1}dy$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, are verbatim the $A$ and $B$ of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]]; the moment $m=\frac12\int y\times J(y)\,dy$ of the lemma is the moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a) ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 2.1 Substituting these identifications into the lemma's conclusion gives the displayed estimates for the framework's $A$ and $B$, with the lemma's uniformity in $n$ and its absolute constants; no additional analysis is required. 2.2 Scope: the estimate is a remainder-controlled far-field expansion; nothing is asserted at smaller radii or at the source, and no empirical content is added. The far-field identification of $m$ as the source moment is exactly the content of this theorem under its hypotheses. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument. The magnetic-moment definition uses a finite Riemann integral on a closed bounding rectangle, whereas the remainder supplier writes the Lebesgue integral. Each smooth compact component of $y\times J(y)$ is bounded Borel and continuous on that rectangle, so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], under the stated Countable Choice, equates them; zero extension gives the same all-space Lebesgue moment.

items.title: Force and torque on a declared ideal thin-wire loop in a prescribed external field
items.statement:
Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$) that is either closed ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(L)$ with matching one-sided derivatives) or a wire segment with free endpoints, let $I\in\mathbb R$, let $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds$ be the finite Riemann source moment defined by this displayed integral in the closed case. For an embedded closed loop this agrees with [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b); embeddedness is not required for the present parametrized-curve calculation. Let $B$ be a prescribed external magnetic field, of class $C^0$ on a neighbourhood of the trace of $\gamma$ in part (a) and of class $C^2$ on an open set containing the closed ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ in parts (b)-(d). Adopt the thin-wire coupling hypothesis (W): for a general closed parametrized curve use the stated direct neutral-wire Riemann coupling (with multiplicity of traversal retained); in the embedded closed-loop specialization its source interpretation is exactly [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1); for an open curve use a compact segment of a fed or closed neutral circuit, including a segment of the declared infinite wire of (c2). Adopt separately for that parametrized wire or local segment the direct external magnetic coupling $dF=I\,d\gamma\times B$ and $dN=\gamma\times dF$, as an ideal extension motivated by the smooth continuum Lorentz law [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii); that smooth-source postulate does not itself include singular currents. An isolated static neutral open segment is not asserted: its standalone current satisfies $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm seg}=I(\delta_{\gamma(0)}-\delta_{\gamma(L)})$, so its endpoint feed/return cannot be suppressed in a global model. Force and torque here concern only the specified local segment under this adopted coupling. Then:

**(a) [Force and torque under (W)]**
$$F:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad N:=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\bigl(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\bigr)\,ds,$$
the componentwise Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,L]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

**(b) [Constant field]** If $\gamma$ is closed and $B$ is constant on a neighbourhood of the loop, then $F=0$ and $N=m\times B$ exactly.

**(c) [Slowly varying field]** Let $\gamma$ be closed with $|\gamma(s)|\le a$ for all $s$, let $B$ be $C^2$ on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with constants $M_1,M_2$ such that $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$, and suppose $\operatorname{div}B=0$ on $B_a(0)$ (as holds for the external part of any smooth-branch vacuum field by [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Then
$$F=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)+R_F,\qquad N=m\times B(0)+R_N,$$
with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|\,L\,a^2M_2$ and $|R_N|\le|I|\,L\,a^2M_1$, where $\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$ is the gradient at $0$ of $x\mapsto m\cdot B(x)$ for the fixed vector $m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**(d) [Sufficient condition]** If the external field is the magnetostatic field of a compact smooth steady current $J_{\rm ext}\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm ext}=0$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]), then it is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and meets the hypotheses of (c) on every ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with finite constants $M_1,M_2$.

**(e) [Scope]** Only the external field acts on the loop: the loop's own field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support and material response are outside the statement, and no claim is made about the loop's dynamics, deformation or failure. The coupling (W) is an explicit idealisation of a neutral thin wire at rest in the laboratory frame; it is adopted, not derived, and the theorem is conditional on it. No measurement or uncertainty is involved. Parts (a)-(c), conditional on the explicit coupling (W) and the supplied curve and external field, are finite Riemann-integral calculations and use no Choice axiom. Part (d), transporting the Newtonian-potential construction, assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct evaluation of the pairings under the coupling, the antisymmetric first-moment identities for a closed curve, one Taylor expansion with an explicit remainder, and the compact-current sufficient condition. 1.1 (a) Under the separately adopted coupling (W), integrate the continuous external force along the compact curve directly in the Riemann sense: $F=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds$, and taking moments gives $N=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s)))\,ds$; both integrands are continuous on $[0,L]$ because $\gamma,\gamma'$ and $B\circ\gamma$ are ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 1.2 (b) For constant $B$, $F=I(\int_0^L\gamma'\,ds)\times B=0$ because $\gamma(L)=\gamma(0)$. For the torque, $\gamma\times(\gamma'\times B)=\gamma'(\gamma\cdot B)-B(\gamma\cdot\gamma')$, so with $M_{jl}:=\int_0^L\gamma_j\gamma'_l\,ds$, $$N=I\int_0^L(\gamma\cdot B)\gamma'\,ds-I B\int_0^L\gamma\cdot\gamma'\,ds=I B_jM_{jl}e_l .$$ The second integral vanishes because $\gamma\cdot\gamma'=\frac12\frac{d}{ds}|\gamma|^2$ integrates to $0$ over a closed curve. For the first, integrating $\frac{d}{ds}(\gamma_j\gamma_l)=0$ over the closed curve gives $M_{jl}+M_{lj}=0$; for such an antisymmetric matrix the moment relation $m_p=\frac I2\varepsilon_{pab}M_{ab}$ is equivalent to $I M_{jl}=\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p$, and substituting this into $I B_jM_{jl}e_l$ and using $B_j\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p e_l=m\times B$ gives $N=m\times B$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

2.1 (c) Write $B(x)=B(0)+DB(0)x+R(x)$ with $|R(x)|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|\le a$; this is the quantitative second-order Taylor hypothesis, the case $k=1$ of [[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]] applied componentwise, with the bound on the Lagrange term supplied by the stated $M_2$. Splitting the force of (a), the constant term vanishes as in (b); the linear term is $I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i$ and, with $I M_{lj}=\varepsilon_{ljp}m_p$, the contraction $\varepsilon_{ijk}\varepsilon_{ljp}=\delta_{kp}\delta_{il}-\delta_{kl}\delta_{ip}$ yields $$I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i=\bigl(\partial_i(m\cdot B)(0)-m_i\operatorname{div}B(0)\bigr)e_i=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0),$$ using $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$; the remainder obeys $|I\int_0^L\gamma'\times R\,ds|\le|I|L\sup_{|x|\le a}|R(x)|\le\frac12|I|La^2M_2$ ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). For the torque, step 1.2 gives $N=m\times B(0)+I\int_0^L\gamma\times(\gamma'\times(B(\gamma)-B(0)))\,ds$, and the remainder is bounded by $|I|\int_0^L|\gamma||\gamma'||B(\gamma)-B(0)|\,ds\le|I|\,a\cdot1\cdot M_1a\cdot L$. This proves (c).

2.2 (d) By [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] the external field of a compact smooth conserved current is $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A$ of class $C^\infty$, hence $B\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$; on a bounded ball the suprema of $|DB|$ and $|D^2B|$ are finite, and the mean-value and second-order Taylor estimates provide the constants $M_1,M_2$ of (c). 2.3 (e) records that (W) is a declared idealisation: only the external field acts, and no self-field, matter model or dynamics enters. Countable Choice is inherited in part (d) through the Newtonian suppliers; parts (a)-(c) use the stated finite Riemann coupling directly and are choice-free. The moment identity follows by contracting two alternating symbols and uses no division by $I$; for $I=0$ the moment, force, torque and both remainders are zero. No scalar distribution action $\langle J,B\rangle$ is equated with a vector force, and continuity rather than smoothness of the external field suffices for the adopted compact-curve Riemann coupling. For an open segment the scalar divergence test gives $-I\int_0^L\frac{d}{ds}\varphi(\gamma(s))ds=I(\varphi(\gamma(0))-\varphi(\gamma(L)))$, the stated endpoint identity. The force/moment algebra applies to all the stated closed parametrized $C^2$ curves, including self-intersecting or multiply traversed curves: closure, unit-speed parametrization and the explicit finite moment integral suffice. Only the embedded closed specialization invokes the ideal-loop source object of the preceding definition.

items.title: Axis field of the declared ideal circular thin loop
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a>0$, $I\in\mathbb R$, let $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$, $s\in[0,2\pi a]$, be the circle of radius $a$ in the plane $x_3=0$ parametrized by arc length, let the declared ideal thin-loop current of amplitude $I$ run along $\gamma$ in the sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1), with moment $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ ([[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b)), and let $\mu_0$, $c$, $\varepsilon_0$ be the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every point $x=ze_3$ on the axis ($z\in\mathbb R$, $\operatorname{dist}(x,\gamma)=\sqrt{a^2+z^2}>0$) the field of the ideal loop is the absolutely convergent line integral
$$B(ze_3)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times\left(ze_3-\gamma(s)\right)}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds=\frac{\mu_0Ia^2}{2(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3,$$
i.e. the Biot-Savart field of [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] and the declared thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] agree on the axis, with the sign fixed by the positive (counterclockwise) orientation of $\gamma$ and by the sign of $I$; in particular $B(0)=\frac{\mu_0I}{2a}e_3$. This is a property of the declared idealisation; it is not the field of any physical finite-radius coil, nothing is claimed at points off the axis or on the wire, and no measurement is involved. The explicit finite Riemann axis evaluation and circle moment calculation alone are choice-free. Countable Choice is inherited by the asserted global distributional model and thin-current supplier.
items.strategy: **Verification.** The circle is a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length, and every axis point lies at distance $\sqrt{a^2+z^2}\ge a>0$ from it, so the field of the declared ideal loop is the Biot-Savart line integral on the axis: the mollified fields of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] converge uniformly on a compact neighbourhood of the axis point to that integral, and [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] identifies the same integral as the field of the compact smooth currents and their declared thin limit. For the evaluation, write $t=s/a$; then $\gamma'(s)=(-\sin t,\cos t,0)$, $ze_3-\gamma(s)=(-a\cos t,-a\sin t,z)$ and $|ze_3-\gamma(s)|=(a^2+z^2)^{1/2}$ is constant, so $$\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))=(z\cos t,\ z\sin t,\ a),$$ and $ds=a\,dt$; hence $$\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds=\frac{a}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\int_0^{2\pi}(z\cos t,z\sin t,a)\,dt=\frac{2\pi a^2}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3,$$ the first two components vanishing by periodicity of $\cos$ and $\sin$ over a full period. Multiplying by $\mu_0I/(4\pi)$ gives the displayed field. Each component is the Riemann integral of a continuous function on the compact interval $[0,2\pi a]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), and the moment $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ is the computation $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b). The example is a conditional ideal-model computation: no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical inference is involved. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument. The global distributional admissibility is supplied separately by the strengthened [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] and the explicit physical adoption [[post-em-ideal-magnetostatic-models]]; the axis integral itself is away from the wire.

items.title: Declared ideal infinite wire and cylindrical current sheet: explicit fields and their distributional equations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]].

**(a) [Ideal infinite straight wire].** Let $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, let $J_{\rm w}$ be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I$ along $\gamma$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and define, on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\gamma$,
$$B(x):=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi\rho}\,e_\varphi,\qquad \rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2},\qquad e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0).$$
Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $\gamma$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $\gamma$; $B$ is invariant under translations along $\gamma$ and rotations about it, and its transverse far-zone supremum tends to $0$ as $\rho\to\infty$; for every $r>0$ and $h\in\mathbb R$, the circulation of $B$ along $\gamma_{r,h}(t)=(r\cos t,r\sin t,h)$, $0\le t\le2\pi$, traversed once with increasing $t$, is $\mu_0I$ ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_{\rm w}$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared wire model; the transverse decay excludes an added homogeneous longitudinal field, and no further selection, uniqueness or energy claim is made.

**(b) [Ideal infinite cylindrical sheet].** Let $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $K\in\mathbb R$, let $J_S$ be the declared ideal sheet current of amplitude $K$ along $S$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c3)), and define $B:=\mu_0Ke_3$ for $\rho<a$ and $B:=0$ for $\rho>a$. Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $S$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $S$; $B$ has the declared symmetry (translations along and rotations about the axis) and its transverse far-zone supremum is $0$; the one-sided jump across $S$, with $n=e_\rho$ from the interior to the exterior and $[B]=B_+-B_-$, is $n\times[B]=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$ and $n\cdot[B]=0$, the stationary tangential-sheet jump for this noncompact cylinder, established by the test-localized [[lem-em-ideal-cylindrical-sheet-field]] for the current density $Ke_\varphi$ (computed directly as $e_\rho\times(0-\mu_0Ke_3)=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_S$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared solenoid model.

**(c) [Scope].** Both models are declared noncompact idealisations: they are not finite-energy localized-current theorems; nothing is asserted about self-energy, inductance, self-force, the fields on the sources, or the approximation of any physical apparatus; and the fields are selected within the declared symmetry and decay class, not shown to be the only solutions of the magnetostatic equations off the sources without that class. The external force between two such wires is treated in [[ex-em-wire-force-coupling]] under the adopted thin-wire coupling.

Circulation is computed only along the positively oriented once-traversed gamma_r,h defined in Example(a). All source values, energy and uniqueness extrapolations remain excluded.

items.title: Force per unit length between two declared ideal parallel wires
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $d>0$ and $I_1,I_2\in\mathbb R$; let wire 1 be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I_1$ along the third coordinate axis and wire 2 the translate of that ideal line current by $d\,e_1$, of amplitude $I_2$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and adopt for the force on wire 2 the thin-wire coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]], restricted to the external field of wire 1. Then the force per unit length on wire 2 is
$$\mathbf f=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_3\times e_2=-\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_1,$$
i.e. attraction towards wire 1 (direction $-e_1$) for currents in the same direction ($I_1I_2>0$), repulsion for opposite directions, and magnitude $\mu_0|I_1I_2|/(2\pi d)$ per unit length. The comparison uses only the external field of wire 1 at the position of wire 2; the self-fields and the mechanical support forces of the two infinite wires are excluded, no claim is made about the total force on either infinite wire, and no measurement is involved.
items.strategy: **Verification.** Wire 1 has the admitted field $B_1=\mu_0I_1/(2\pi\rho)\,e_\varphi$ of [[ex-em-infinite-wire-and-solenoid]](a), which at the points $(d,0,x_3)$ of wire 2 takes the constant value $B_1=\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi d}\,e_2$ (there $e_\varphi=e_2$). By the coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]](a) applied to the compact straight segments $\{(d,0,x_3):|x_3|\le S\}$ of wire 2 (with arc-length parameter $x_3$ and $|\gamma'|=1$), the force on the segment is $$I_2\int_{-S}^{S}e_3\times B_1\,dx_3=2S\,\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,(e_3\times e_2),$$ the Riemann integral of a constant continuous integrand over a compact interval ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Dividing by the length $2S$ gives the force per unit length of the displayed form, independent of $S$; the sign of $I_1I_2$ gives attraction or repulsion as stated. Only the external field of wire 1 is used, and the self-field of wire 2 and the support forces of both infinite wires are excluded; the computation is a local external-force comparison, not a solution of the two-wire dynamics, and involves no measurement. The preceding same-B-page example is a permitted intra-page supplier and its corrected proof uses the A-level ideal-line lemma and explicit model adoption. The compact segment uses the separately adopted local coupling, with the return/feed outside the force segment; no isolated neutral open segment is claimed to be globally conserved. Countable Choice is inherited by the asserted ideal-line model, while the final constant-force Riemann calculation is finite.
